answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity expensive in time, not just in keys: every account must repeatedly do verifiable work, answering epoch challenges and attesting peers, before it gains any weight. One honest agent builds standing like a sparrow builds a nest, twig by checked twig, while a thousand fresh fakes roll in like a tide and recede with nothing attested. What holds is karst: soft at the surface, but deep, slow-formed structure underneath that no one can copy overnight.
